overviews: This paper investigates adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 fuzzy cyber-physical systems subject to deception attacks and actuator failures. A membership-function-derivative-dependent switching design and a looped-functional approach are developed for controller synthesis, and two examples are presented. The topic is relevant to secure networked control. The following minor points should be addressed to improve the presentation of the manuscript.

This manuscript considers the joint design of fuzzy controllers and an adaptive event-triggering mechanism for cyber-physical systems with deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. The analysis uses membership-function derivative information and a two-sided looped functional to obtain LMI-based design conditions. The problem is of interest. Some explanations of the design methodology could be improved, as detailed below.

The paper studies adaptive event-triggered control of interval type-2 fuzzy systems under cyberattacks and actuator failures. The proposed design is illustrated by a PMSM example and a numerical example. The manuscript would benefit from clearer discussion of the simulation results and the scope of the conclusions. My specific comments are as follows.

language.old: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) affected by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. Since nonlinear CPSs face cyber-layer attacks as well as physical-layer component failures, while their communication resources are often limited, an adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) is employed to reduce redundant network transmissions through dynamic adjustment of the triggering threshold based on real-time state-error information. Specifically, stochastic deception attacks are characterized by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are modeled by Markov switching fault matrices. Accordingly, a unified closed-loop model is established. Then, a looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) is constructed to exploit membership-function information and sampled-data dynamics. Based on this functional, stability criteria are obtained to guarantee asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level. Moreover, joint design of the controller gains and adaptive triggering parameters is formulated through tractable linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Validation is finally carried out with an engineering-motivated permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy system to demonstrate the effectiveness and feasibility of the developed method.
language.new: This article addresses adaptive event-triggered control for interval type-2 (IT-2) fuzzy cyber-physical systems (CPSs) subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An adaptive event-triggered mechanism (AETM) adjusts the transmission threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant communication. Deception attacks are described by a Bernoulli process, and actuator failures are represented by Markov switching fault matrices. These components are incorporated into a unified closed-loop model. The signs of the membership-function derivatives define operational regions for a region-dependent fuzzy controller. Within this framework, the controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly designed. A two-sided looped functional dependent on fuzzy membership functions (FMFs) incorporates membership information and sampled-data dynamics. Sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability with a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_\infty$ disturbance attenuation level are formulated as linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). A permanent magnet synchronous motor example and a numerical IT-2 fuzzy example illustrate the control responses and the reduction in data transmissions.

language.old: This study has addressed adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs affected simultaneously by stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. An AETM has been employed to limit unnecessary data transmissions by updating the triggering threshold online using real-time state-error information. In addition, a region-dependent piecewise fuzzy control strategy has been developed by incorporating derivative information from the membership functions. Based on an FMF-dependent and time-dependent looped functional, stability criteria have been obtained to guarantee closed-loop asymptotic stability while achieving a prescribed $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ disturbance attenuation level. The controller gains and adaptive event-triggering weight matrices have been jointly determined through tractable LMIs, while a bounding technique has been employed to address the norm-bounded uncertainty induced by Markov-type actuator failures.
language.new: This study has considered adaptive event-triggered $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ control of IT-2 fuzzy CPSs subject to stochastic deception attacks and Markov-type actuator failures. The AETM updates its threshold using state-error information to reduce redundant transmissions. Membership-function derivative information defines operational regions for the fuzzy control design. An FMF-dependent looped functional is used to formulate sufficient stability and performance conditions. The controller gains and event-triggering weight matrices are jointly determined through LMIs, with a bounding technique used to handle actuator-failure uncertainty.
